findings.summary: CPU preflight records training and requires_grad_any for each checkpoint but never asserts them, and always writes status passed.
findings.trigger: A checkpoint load returns a model with training=True or any parameter requires_grad=True (for example a regression in worker.load_inference_model) while the load itself does not raise.
findings.consequence: cpu-preflight.json still says status passed. launch_once.py:106 gates only on status == passed and mps_operations == 0, so the launcher claims the one-shot marker and spawns probe.py. probe.py later rejects the model (its strict CPU check) only after the marker is consumed. The registered gate 'strict CPU loads' is therefore not enforced where the launcher decides, and a one-shot registration is burned.
findings.fix: Assert not training and no requires_grad in cpu_preflight.run before writing the receipt, or have launch_once.py check strict_cpu_loads[*].training is false and requires_grad_any is false and that module_origins are present, before claim_once.

findings.summary: MPS driver cap (6 GiB) is enforced only inside guard() at evaluate boundaries; the sampler thread records MPS values without enforcing the cap, and the launcher RSS monitor does not read MPS at all.
findings.trigger: MPS driver allocation exceeds 6 GiB during a forward or evaluate segment that has no guard call before the launcher's 110-second child_timeout (launch_once.py child_timeout).
findings.consequence: The over-cap condition is not detected while it occurs. It is detected only at the next guard call, or the probe runs until the 110-second bound. The plan text says separate caps are enforced during work; enforcement is only as frequent as guard cadence. I did not verify guard cadence inside worker.evaluate, so the exposure window is unquantified. The unit test test_inflight_mps_cap_fails_on_numeric_driver_overage covers the value check only, not an in-flight overage between guards.

findings.summary: On a normal child exit, a surviving owned process group member raises RuntimeError without any signal or cleanup evidence.
findings.trigger: probe.py exits 0 while a descendant process remains in the owned PGID.
findings.consequence: The leftover process is not terminated by the launcher. The failure path records process_group_absent None and absence_status unknown, which is truthful, but the bounded exact-owned cleanup gate is not exercised here. probe.py spawns no children, so the trigger is narrow.
